evaluation: Forward-chained (rolling-origin) validation: four consecutive 2-week test blocks (3 Apr - 1 Jun 2023), each scored on the 15-min bins of that block after training only on data ending 1 h before the block, with exactly the same causal feature code and the 1-hour-ahead rule (last usable 5-min row = T-50 min). Pooled RMSE of the final ET+gradient-boosting blend was 36.4 ppm (blocks: ~45, ~46, ~27, ~26 ppm) versus 40.5 ppm for the 'last 15-min mean' persistence baseline; the final model is trained on all 3 months, so the estimate is slightly conservative for periods similar to May (RMSE ~26) but the error scales with occupancy, so a range of roughly 22 ppm (quiet summer) to 45 ppm (busy teaching weeks) is plausible; 34 is the central estimate.
data_findings: File is semicolon separated, UTF-8 with BOM, '#N/A' for missing, and timestamps carry a UTC offset (+0100 before 26 Mar 2023, +0200 after, DST switch present). I parse the offset and do all lag/cut-off logic on the UTC time line (so the 45-minute rule holds across DST changes), and output tz-naive local time labels; if a local hour is repeated in autumn only the first labelled copy is returned.

Rows are not in time order: 29 rows on 2023-04-24 (13:05-15:30) are stored in reversed order, and the block 2023-05-24 23:05 to 2023-05-25 23:00 appears twice (identical copies, 288 duplicated timestamps). I sort by time and keep the first copy of each timestamp.

Gaps: the first hour of the file (all columns NA except People__amount); a 12 h hole on 2 Apr (07:40-19:45); a few isolated single-row NAs. Missing values are never interpolated or back-filled (that would use future data): forward fill is limited to 3 h for CO2 (1 h for status signals) and the model handles remaining NaN natively; if no CO2 is available for 3 h a calendar/same-time-yesterday fallback model is used.

Sentinels / junk: CO2 contains 15 values of -999 (set to missing; fixed physical validity range 250-6000 ppm), the wind column contains the text 'OFFLINE' (coerced to NaN), outdoor temperature has 8 isolated spikes of 57-73 degC (set to NaN with a fixed -45..45 degC limit). One isolated CO2 spike of 1521 ppm on 21 Apr is real-looking and kept (it cannot be forecast).

RoomB room temperature sensor failed on 2023-05-12 10:00 and reads 72-83 degC from then until the end of the file; it was therefore not used as a feature (it would be a regime shift). People__amount is NA for ~62% of rows (several March stretches and everything from 14 Apr on) so it is unusable; setpoint / heating-limit / cooling-limit columns are constant (22 / 20.5 / 23.5) and carry no information.

The CO2 signal is a change-of-value log: it is held constant (95% of consecutive 5-min values are identical) and moves in ~50 ppm steps. This quantisation (+-25 ppm timing/step noise on every 15-min mean) plus unforecastable occupancy changes (largest errors 16-18 h when people leave, 8-11 h when they arrive) gives an irreducible error floor; the best model is only ~10% better than persistence. Room level signals follow a weekday office pattern (CO2 about 420-450 ppm baseline, 500-1000 ppm when occupied, near-flat on weekends and Danish public holidays such as Easter 6-10 Apr, 5 May, 18 May and 29 May).

Model: residual (target minus last observed 15-min mean) ExtraTrees (2 seeds) + gradient boosting on only causal features: lagged CO2 levels/changes/rolling stats up to 7 days, same-time-of-day CO2 from the previous 1-7 days (all taken from windows that end before T-45 min), time since last change, hour/weekday and Danish holiday flags. Outdoor-weather and room-status (occupancy flag, window, light, damper, fan) features gave no cross-validated gain and were dropped for robustness against seasonal drift. Training used every 5-min origin (3x more rows). Causality was verified by truncating the file / replacing all rows from the cut-off onward with garbage and confirming identical forecasts (max difference 1e-13) for all intervals up to 45 minutes after the cut-off.
